checkpoints.question: Which type of VPN requires client software to be installed on the endpoint and is user-initiated rather than always-on?

options.A: Remote access VPN using client-based software
options.B: Site-to-site VPN connecting two full networks
options.C: MPLS circuit VPN replacing dedicated private bandwidth
options.D: Clientless remote access VPN using a web browser

checkpoints.explanation: Client-based remote access VPN installs software like Cisco AnyConnect on the endpoint and is initiated by the user, contrasting with site-to-site VPNs which are always-on and require no client software.

checkpoints.section: IPsec — the protocol suite behind most VPNs
checkpoints.question: Which IPsec component provides both encryption and authentication of the payload?

options.A: IKE (Internet Key Exchange) which negotiates algorithms and exchanges keys
options.B: Diffie-Hellman which derives a shared secret over untrusted channels
options.C: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) which encrypts payload and authenticates
options.D: AH (Authentication Header) which proves sender identity without encrypting

checkpoints.explanation: ESP is the component that actually provides VPN confidentiality by encrypting the payload and authenticating it; AH alone is almost never used in VPNs.

checkpoints.section: IPsec — the protocol suite behind most VPNs
checkpoints.question: In IPsec tunnel mode, what is encrypted compared to transport mode?

options.A: Only the original destination IP address while the source remains visible
options.B: The entire original packet including both header and payload in a new packet
options.C: Only the payload data while data center server addresses stay exposed
options.D: Only the payload while the original IP header remains visible to observers

checkpoints.explanation: Tunnel mode encrypts the entire original IP packet (header and payload) and wraps it in a new packet, whereas transport mode encrypts only the payload and leaves headers visible.

checkpoints.question: Why is SSL/TLS VPN more commonly used for remote access in hotels and coffee shops?

options.A: It uses MPLS circuits which are designed for mobile device connectivity and access
options.B: It does not require encryption which makes it faster than IPsec in most environments
options.C: It uses UDP 500 which is open through most firewall rules and allows quick connections
options.D: It runs on TCP port 443 which is almost always open through firewalls for HTTPS traffic

checkpoints.explanation: SSL/TLS VPN uses TCP port 443 (standard HTTPS) which firewalls almost always leave open, making it firewall-friendly compared to IPsec which uses UDP ports and the ESP protocol that may be blocked.

checkpoints.question: What is the security risk of split tunneling?

options.A: Only corporate traffic goes through encryption while all other traffic remains visible
options.B: All corporate traffic is forced through the VPN tunnel which increases overall bandwidth costs
options.C: Internet traffic bypasses VPN controls and malware can use a direct path to reach servers
options.D: The VPN connection is automatically established at boot time and never disconnects

checkpoints.explanation: Split tunneling allows internet traffic to bypass corporate controls, creating a risk where malware on a client could use the direct internet path to contact a command-and-control server while the VPN remains active.

checkpoints.question: Why was RSA key exchange removed from TLS 1.3?

options.A: It lacked Perfect Forward Secrecy and allowed past sessions to decrypt if the private key was compromised
options.B: It required multiple handshake round trips and caused slower connection establishment times
options.C: It was vulnerable to the BEAST attack and required immediate removal from the protocol
options.D: It was replaced by AES-GCM cipher which offers faster and more efficient encryption capabilities

checkpoints.explanation: RSA key exchange did not provide PFS, meaning if a server's private key was ever compromised, all past encrypted sessions using that key could be retroactively decrypted.

checkpoints.question: Which SSH authentication method is immune to brute-force attacks?

options.A: Port forwarding which tunnels other protocols through the encrypted SSH connection
options.B: Public key authentication where the private key never leaves the client
options.C: Password authentication where the encrypted password is sent in the SSH session
options.D: Telnet-based authentication which replaced cleartext credentials with encryption

checkpoints.explanation: Public key authentication is immune to brute-force and password capture because the private key never leaves the client and is not transmitted, whereas password auth is vulnerable to both.

checkpoints.question: What is the main advantage of SFTP over FTPS for new deployments?

options.A: SFTP uses explicit mode on port 21 which is easier to configure than implicit FTPS mode
options.B: SFTP is an extension of FTP with TLS encryption added on top of the base protocol
options.C: SFTP supports both explicit and implicit modes which provides maximum compatibility options
options.D: SFTP runs on SSH and uses one port through a firewall while FTPS uses separate control and data channels

checkpoints.explanation: SFTP is preferred because it runs over SSH on port 22 (a single port) and simplifies firewall rules, whereas FTPS (standard FTP with TLS) uses separate control and data channels that complicate firewall configuration.
